video.title: Make Money With This New AI Agent That Works 24/7

summary: Chris Koerner tries the agentic AI tool he calls 'Grok Bot' for the first time and uses it to build a 'Morning Lock' product: a Mac menu bar app plus Chrome extension that locks Gmail and the Mail app outside set hours (e.g. 5-10am), with an accountability password held by a spouse. He had Claude write the prompt, then Grok Bot built, tested and fixed the app via Replit, GitHub and Stripe in about 31 minutes of recording. He says he plans to sell it as a SaaS in a part two, but no sales or revenue are shown. The takeaway is that agentic AI can produce a working, personally useful software product from one detailed prompt; whether it sells is untested.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; builds the app on screen

speakers.name: Billy

ideas.name: Morning Lock: email/website time-lock app (Mac app + Chrome extension) sold as SaaS
ideas.one_liner: A productivity app that blocks Gmail, the Mac Mail app and chosen distracting sites outside set hours, with an accountability password held by a spouse or friend.
ideas.business_model: SaaS subscription sold via a website with Stripe payments (planned, not yet launched)
ideas.customer: Knowledge workers and people who struggle with inbox management or distraction and want forced time-boxing
ideas.problem: Calendar time-boxing is hard to stick to because nobody else is accountable; people get distracted and fall behind on email.
ideas.offer: Mac menu bar app plus Chrome extension that locks Gmail/Mail (and other chosen apps and sites) outside defined windows, lets users block most-visited sites, and sends the unlock password to a spouse or loved one.

pricing.model: SaaS subscription planned; no price stated
pricing.notes: Selling is deferred to 'part two'; no pricing discussed.

acquisition_channels.details: Implied: Koerner would sell to his YouTube audience; he says selling will be covered in part two. No channel plan is given.

ideas.delivery: Software built by the AI agent (Grok Bot) driving Replit and GitHub. Chrome extension and Mac app are downloaded and installed by the user. Human steps needed: Apple developer account and Chrome Web Store developer account (about 20 minutes, per Claude).
unit_economics_claims: Build took about 31 minutes 37 seconds of recording time
Grok Bot was authorised to approve Replit overages up to $100 per day
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated beyond Replit usage, capped at $100 per day in the prompt; Apple and Chrome developer account fees not stated

acquisition.how: Nothing is planned yet. Realistically SEO, content and app-store listings could be agent-driven, but this is unproven in the video.

onboarding.how: Self-serve download and install, with Stripe checkout and a password setup flow; a browser extension install and Mac permissions need some user effort.

delivery.how: The product is software; the agent built and tested it. Distribution through the Apple and Chrome stores needs one-off human account setup and review handling.

billing.how: Stripe subscriptions run unattended once configured.

support.how: Bugs and OS or browser updates will need agent triage with human oversight; an LLM support bot can handle routine questions.

uk_applicability.notes: Software product with no US-specific dependency. UK needs normal VAT, GDPR and app-store compliance. Chrome extension and Mac app distribution works the same.

risks: Unvalidated demand: no customers or sales yet
Crowded market of website and app blockers
Mac and Chrome updates may break the blocking
Password-unlock design may be easy to bypass, and the extension reads browsing history, raising privacy and GDPR concerns
Agent-built code is untested at scale and may have security bugs
App-store review and developer account friction

tactics.name: Have Claude write the agent prompt
steps: Describe the product, constraints and goal to Claude in plain English
Ask for a 'Grok Bot friendly' prompt using the technical terms you don't know
Include build-test-fix loops, a spend cap and a request that the agent asks for the credentials it needs
Paste the prompt into the agent and walk away

quote.text: Write a beautiful prompt that is Grokbot friendly using all the technical coding terms I know nothing about
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Manage the agent like an employee
steps: Give the agent a job and focus rather than micromanaging step by step
Connect only the integrations it needs (here Stripe test mode, GitHub, Replit)

quote.text: A good boss says, "This is your job. Just do this. Just focus on this."
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Iterate with short follow-up prompts
steps: Add features with one-line prompts, e.g. list most-used sites and apps for easy blocking
Report bugs briefly (e.g. 'the icon doesn't work') and let the agent fix them

warnings.warning: Some steps cannot be done by an agent: creating the Apple developer account and Chrome Web Store developer account, and a website alone cannot force-quit a Mac app, so a native Mac app plus extension is needed.

quote.text: Two things an AI agent physically cannot do for you, create your Apple developer account and your Chrome Web Store dev account.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Don't connect the agent to everything; limit its access to what it needs.

quote.text: I don't want it to do a bunch of stuff.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Build tools to solve your own problem first; a product you actually use is the best early validation and a source of content.

quote.text: I want to build it for myself cuz I think this will help me be more productive. But I think I could also sell it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use a stronger model to critique the plan before handing it to an agent; Claude caught that Replit web apps cannot lock a Mac mail app.

quote.text: A website can never force quit your mail app.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Accountability works better with a third party or money at stake than with a self-made calendar block.

quote.text: it's hard for me to be accountable to a calendar event that no other human is a part of
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Agent autonomy needs guardrails: spend caps, test mode for payments and limited integrations.
Building is now cheap, so the bottleneck shifts to distribution; he defers selling to a part two, and demand is unproven.

quote.text: Now, I need to sell it. That's going to be on part two.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Test the habit or demand cheaply before building (Claude suggested testing the habit first for $0).

evidence_quality.rationale: A first-hand live demo of building a product, but there are no sales, revenue or customer evidence, and the build is a single novelty test. The app is useful as a proof of agent capability only; the commercial case is speculation.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes his Playmakers.ai paid community; says the video is not sponsored by Grok Bot.
